entries.answer: An integer is a whole number with no fractional part, and it includes zero and the negative numbers, which is where everyday speech is narrower than the mathematical sense. People often use whole number to mean positive only, and then the two words stop being interchangeable. Integers are the only values a computer stores exactly, so 0.1 plus 0.2 is not 0.3 even though it prints that way, and the error is small but permanent.

entries.answer: A decimal number is written in base ten with a point separating the whole part from the fraction, and it is the notation almost the whole world uses for arithmetic. The word also names a small fraction of something, as in a tenth of a cent, so the two senses sit a long way apart. The practical difference from a fraction is place value, because 0.5 and 0.05 are a single value in fraction arithmetic and entirely different numbers written as decimals.

patterns: how to tell odd from even
entries.answer: An odd number is one that leaves a remainder of one when divided by two, and the same word also means strange, unusual or unmatched. English is full of overlaps like this and the mathematical sense is the older, appearing long before the word was applied to anything eccentric. Nothing beyond the last digit decides it, and that digit has to be 1, 3, 5, 7 or 9, so the test needs no division at all.

patterns: how to check if a number is even
entries.answer: An even number divides by two with no remainder, and the same word also means level, fair or smooth. Here too the older sense is the arithmetical one, and the everyday sense arrived by way of describing something flat rather than by separate invention. Only the final character matters, and it has to be 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8, which is why the whole test fits in one glance.

patterns: how do you write a negative
entries.answer: A negative number is less than zero, and it carries a sign rather than being a separate kind of quantity, which is why the minus is written in front instead of being subtracted. The word also means unfavourable, as in a negative result, and that overlap is exactly why a negative medical result is worth stating in plain words. Arithmetically both signs are present, and the single point that separates them is what defines which is which.

entries.answer: A digit is one symbol from 0 to 9, and a number is a string of them, so seven is a single digit and seventeen is two. English blurs the pair constantly, because most people say number when they mean digit and nothing breaks until place value comes up. The distinction carries real weight in mathematics teaching, where counting digits is a different exercise from counting numbers, and in computing, where a numeric type is described by how many digits it holds.
